text:
sec-bot: EDR alert on host emily-m1 (macOS arm64) — suspicious helper process 'credential-helperd' invoked `/usr/bin/security` and attempted keychain writes. File quarantined: /usr/local/bin/credential-helperd. severity: high. hash: sha256=3f5a9c...; PID=4128.

samir: @jordan can you isolate the device from network and mark for live response?

jordan: on it. serial? can you confirm which user?

sec-bot: owner: emily.l@redwood.com, serial: C02XG0X7G, quarantined by EDR at 2026-03-19T14:02:14Z. Observed DNS beacons to `cdn-uploads.info`.

emily: ugh. I installed a notes helper yesterday from a web installer — not from our MDM. Laptop is on my desk, still logged in. Should I reboot?

samir: please DO NOT reboot. @emily leave it plugged in but disconnected from Wi‑Fi. @jordan disable network access from the MDM console and remove any VPN creds.

jordan: disabling network now and starting live session. Asking user to lock screen and avoid touching USBs.

samir: For live response please run (as admin):
```
# run from secure terminal
sudo /usr/local/bin/edrctl live-collect --pid 4128 --output /tmp/emily_live.tgz
sudo /usr/local/bin/edrctl live-scan --full --output /tmp/emily_scan.json
shasum -a 256 /usr/local/bin/credential-helperd
```

dana: also collect macOS diagnostic package (sysdiagnose) and keychain dump (careful with creds):
```
sudo sysdiagnose -f /tmp/sysdiag_emily && sudo /usr/bin/security dump-keychain /Users/emily/Library/Keychains/login.keychain-db > /tmp/keychain_dump.txt
```

samir: thanks. @jordan upload the artifacts to the incident vault (secure-s3 path). then run a network capture (30s) from edr.

jordan: artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-incidents/1820001234/emily_live.tgz, scan results in JSON. quick grep found outgoing DNS to `cdn-uploads.info` and IP 45.79.160.12.

samir: I pulled the binary hash — not in allowlist or VirusTotal enterprise. Behavior: spawns `/usr/bin/security` with `-w` flag and writes to login.keychain-db. That indicates credential harvesting. recommend immediate credential rotation for emily and any service tokens used on that machine.

emily: ok — I can rotate passwords. What about my laptop — do you want it reimaged?

samir: yes. Given keychain tampering and a non-managed installer, we should reimage. Steps: 1) backup user data (encrypted Time Machine to company vault), 2) revoke machine cert and MDM token, 3) wipe and re-enroll via MDM.

jordan: coordinating pickup with emily now. advising encrypted backup only, no direct copy of system files.

dana: follow-ups for the incident ticket: rotate any OAuth tokens that were accessible, add `3f5a9c...` to IOC list, block `cdn-uploads.info` and IPs at perimeter, update detection signature to catch helpers invoking `/usr/bin/security`. assign postmortem owner.

samir: assigning postmortem to @dana. Also enable elevated logging for Keychain access events for the org and check KMS/HSM audit logs for unusual decrypt operations tied to emily's account.

dana: noted. I'll run an audit of KMS logs for the last 48h and escalate if any keys were used.

emily: thanks team — I'll plug in for backup and hand laptop to @jordan in 30m.

jordan: got it. Outbound blocks in place, device isolated, reimage scheduled.

samir: closing live investigation. Will open a follow-up thread with postmortem and remediation timeline once KMS/audit checks are done. :white_check_mark:

dana: thumbs up. adding action items to the incident tracker. :spiral_note_pad:
